rationale: Tests application of initial stabilisation priorities in the poisoned patient at GCS threshold for intubation
Tests understanding of the cholinergic toxidrome features to distinguish it from the sympathomimetic toxidrome
Tests recall of Datura stramonium toxidrome features as a key plant poisoning in India
Tests critical management principle in corrosive poisoning — contraindication of gastric lavage/vomiting
Tests application of Rumack-Matthew nomogram timing and NAC initiation threshold in paracetamol overdose
Tests understanding of naloxone as the specific antidote for opioid overdose and its mechanism
Tests the correct atropine titration endpoint in organophosphate poisoning — a critical known trap
Tests understanding of intermediate syndrome timing and its distinction from cholinergic crisis
Tests the critical knowledge that aluminium phosphide poisoning has NO antidote — a key exam trap
Tests understanding of the mechanism of phosphine toxicity and its resulting cardiovascular effects
Tests application of the correct antidote (fomepizole/ethanol) for methanol poisoning — must match ADH inhibition mechanism
Tests analysis of the diagnostic value of osmolar gap vs anion gap in early vs late methanol poisoning
Tests application of medico-legal case obligations — every poisoning is an MLC in India
Tests understanding of mandatory psychiatric consultation criteria after deliberate self-poisoning
